students who failed a diagnostic writing test and took a writing skills course improved their writing skills, as evidenced by their performance on a subsequent gateway media writing course.

the LSDT is a valid predictor of student writing skills, that the writing course is an effective means for improving student writing skills, and that students who take the writing course are more successful in the gateway media course.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found the writing diagnostic to be a useful tool in assessing student writing and identifying students in need of writing assistance.
the writing diagnostic test has been successful in identifying students who need remedial work and in improving their writing skills.

we found a significant difference between the writing skills of students who failed the test and those who passed it, and a significant difference between students who passed the test and took the writing course and those who did not take the writing course.

the writing diagnostic tests we developed are a useful tool for identifying students who need help in developing writing skills, and the writing remediation course we created is an effective tool for teaching basic writing skills to these students.
